overall: Atlanta is experiencing a heavily overcast morning (OVC, ceiling ~400 ft / 122m) that has completely stalled temperature rise — the running max of 73.4°F was set at midnight and temperatures have barely moved since, sitting at 71.6°F with zero warming velocity at 9:35 AM. This is a notably sluggish start for a mid-June day where solar heating should be well underway by now. The high dewpoint (69.8°F) indicates a very moist, stable airmass keeping a lid on temperatures.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models (ECMWF 86.0°F, HRRR 85.2°F, NBM 86.4°F) show tight agreement in the 85–86°F range, running about 2°F below the NWS text forecast of 88°F — that gap likely reflects the models' better handling of the persistent morning cloud deck. max_temp_prediction: The dominant scenario is a high in the 86–87°F range: the META model peaks there at 37%, NWP models average ~85.9°F, and the prolonged morning overcast (which typically steals 1–3°F from the daily high via lost solar insolation) makes the NWS 88°F target a stretch. The best-case scenario for 88°F requires clouds to break decisively by early afternoon and heating to compress into a narrower afternoon window ahead of the 5 PM storm chance. Confidence is moderate-to-good on 85–87°F; overall estimate is 86.5°F.
